newsitem.title: UK: SHOWERS DISRUPT UK GRAINS HARVESTING.
newsitem.headline: SHOWERS DISRUPT UK GRAINS HARVESTING.

text.p: Showers, with some thunderstorms, spreading north through England overnight had disrupted the stop-start grains harvest in many areas, farming sources said.
In most places, however, the crop should dry off and the fast progress made at the start of the week resume fairly quickly. "They were motoring (before the rain)", one farming analyst said.
In parts of the South-West the rain brought work to a halt.
Work on farms along the north coast area of Cornwall had stopped completely, John Cowling, a farmer based near Newquay, told Reuters.

"According to my gauge we had 10 millimetres of rain overnight," he said. Weather conditions this morning were not good for drying the crop and he did not expect work to restart soon. "We've got no wind and very little sun," he said.
Another source on a farm in the east of the county said that work there had also stopped. Good progress was being made until late Tuesday, she said.
On the other side of the country, heavy rain in East Anglia was likely to cause little more than a hiccup in the harvest, sources there indicated.

"We had quite a lot of rain overnight," one analyst in Norfolk said. But, with the sun shining, she expected it to cause no more than a temporary delay. "I imagine people will be back harvesting from this afternoon."
Apart from causing a slight delay to the harvest, the rain was generally welcomed by East Anglian farmers, who had suffered from water shortages, she said.
